meta.description: Runs cis-pQTL Mendelian randomization for drug-target validation using UKB-PPP (Olink), deCODE (SomaScan), Fenland, INTERVAL, ARIC, and FinnGen-PPP proteomes plus colocalization triangulation, phenome-wide on-target adverse-effect scans, cross-platform Olink/SomaScan replication, and PAV (protein-altering variant) sensitivity.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 7 inputs use explicitly-labeled synthetic, planted-ground-truth data; no fabricated DOI/PMID/trial results or invented real-world statistics appear in any output.

practice_boundaries.detail: Workflow is population-level drug-target genomics research (gate 7 in scope); no individual diagnostic or prescriptive claim appears in any of the 7 outputs.

methodological_ground.detail: No correlation-causation conflation; the skill's own triangulation ladder was empirically validated (Input 6: trans-pQTL inclusion demonstrably distorts the estimate 3.6x; Input 7: a bare nominal p-value is correctly refused as insufficient for a drug-target claim).

code_usability.detail: 6 of 7 inputs executed real R code to completion with checkable numeric results against planted ground truth. One real defect was found and reproduced (Input 5: TwoSampleMR/MendelianRandomization mr_ivw namespace collision) but it fails loudly with a one-line fix, not silently or unrunnably -- does not meet the M4 FAIL bar; recorded as a P1 recommendation instead.

functional_suitability.note: Covers single-target cis-MR, phewas, cross-platform replication, correlated/robust IVW, allelic heterogeneity (coloc.susie), PAV sensitivity, and sample-overlap correction -- essentially the full stated scope. Docked 1 point for the undocumented mr_ivw namespace collision found in execution testing (Input 5).

reliability.note: Common-Errors table (11 rows) and an explicit Version-Compatibility section instructing the agent to introspect installed APIs rather than blindly retry are strong fault-tolerance features (Category-3 hard-stop-is-correct override applied). Neither covers the mr_ivw masking failure or the phewas example's own debug-shortcut anti-pattern.

performance_context.note: usage-guide.md separates quick-start from the main SKILL.md, but SKILL.md itself (450 lines, no references/ subfolder) carries the entire methodological corpus -- decision trees, thresholds, failure modes -- inline rather than deferring the denser tables.

agent_usability.note: Exceptionally explicit worked examples with exact hg38 coordinates and function calls; consistent column-naming (SNP/BETA/SE/A1/A2/EAF/P) throughout; Common-Errors + Anticipated-Reviewer-Pushback tables give strong preventive guidance. Docked 1 point: no warning anywhere about the TwoSampleMR/MendelianRandomization mr_ivw name collision central to its own correlated-IV workflow.

human_usability.note: Description and Quick-Start prompts use natural researcher phrasing ('nominate or de-risk a drug target', 'mimic pharmacological inhibition'), though dense and expert-jargon-heavy by nature of the domain. Strict-input-validation Category-3 override applied to forgiveness.

security.note: No hardcoded credentials, no injection vectors; file-path-based local TSV reads are appropriate for a research-analysis skill; no PHI/PII in scope (aggregate GWAS summary statistics).

maintainability.note: Two example scripts are well-scoped and separable, but neither ships with self-contained/synthetic data -- both hardcode local paths (ukbppp_pcsk9.tsv, 1kg_EUR/EUR) that require the user's own real data or an auditor-built substitute (as this audit did) to actually run, limiting out-of-the-box testability.

agent_specific.note: Precise, non-overlapping trigger description relative to sibling skills (mendelian-randomization, pleiotropy-detection, colocalization-analysis); 10-entry Related-Skills cross-reference; explicit, empirically-validated escape hatches (trans-pQTL refusal, cross-platform-disagreement non-claim, sample-overlap correction). Docked for SKILL.md length/layering (8.2) relative to the ≤500-line-with-references ideal.

recommendations.title: mr_ivw namespace collision between TwoSampleMR and MendelianRandomization
recommendations.problem: When coloc, MendelianRandomization, and TwoSampleMR are all loaded (a natural combination for the correlated cis-IVW + coloc.susie workflow this skill documents), TwoSampleMR::mr_ivw silently shadows MendelianRandomization::mr_ivw on the search path if TwoSampleMR loads last. The documented call mr_ivw(mr_obj, model='default', correl=TRUE) then throws 'unused arguments' with no hint of the real cause.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's 'Cis-IVW with Correlated Instruments' and 'Robust/Penalized cis-IVW' code blocks never use explicit MendelianRandomization:: namespacing, and no Common-Errors row warns about this cross-package name collision.
recommendations.fix: Add explicit MendelianRandomization::mr_ivw() calls in both code blocks, and add a row to the Common Errors table: "mr_ivw() throws 'unused arguments' | TwoSampleMR::mr_ivw masks MendelianRandomization::mr_ivw when both are loaded | call MendelianRandomization::mr_ivw() explicitly."

recommendations.title: Shipped phewas example contains the exact debug shortcut its own SKILL.md text disclaims
recommendations.problem: examples/phewas_drug_target_mr.R runs lapply(outcomes_filt$id[1:200], scan_one_outcome) as its literal example code, while SKILL.md's prose a few lines below calls this same [1:200] pattern 'a debug shortcut, not a defensible pheWAS protocol.'
recommendations.root_cause: The cautionary note was added to SKILL.md's prose without updating the actual shipped example it refers to.
recommendations.fix: Remove the [1:200] slice from examples/phewas_drug_target_mr.R (loop over the full outcomes_filt$id) or replace it with a clearly-marked, commented-out debug line so the copy-pasteable example matches the documented best practice.

recommendations.title: No concrete path to a local LD reference panel
recommendations.problem: The correlated cis-IVW and clumping workflow hard-depends on genetics.binaRies (GitHub-only install) plus a 1kg_EUR/EUR bfile that the skill never shows how to obtain or build; with OpenGWAS gated, an agent has no documented fallback for real in-window LD.
recommendations.root_cause: The skill assumes either live OpenGWAS access or a pre-existing local 1000G reference, neither of which is guaranteed.
recommendations.fix: Add a concrete recipe (e.g. plink2 --make-bed from public 1000G phase 3 VCFs restricted to the EUR superpopulation) so an agent without OpenGWAS access can still build a real reference panel.

recommendations.title: SKILL.md carries the full methodological corpus inline with no references/ split
recommendations.problem: At ~450 lines with dense decision-tree, threshold, and reconciliation tables, SKILL.md exceeds the progressive-disclosure ideal of a concise top-level file with depth deferred to references/.
recommendations.root_cause: No references/ subfolder exists; usage-guide.md only separates quick-start prompts, not the methodological tables.
recommendations.fix: Move the Data Source Taxonomy, Cis-MR Methodological Taxonomy, Quantitative Thresholds, and Reconciliation tables into a references/ subfolder, leaving SKILL.md as a shorter router into them.

recommendations.title: Example scripts are not runnable out-of-the-box
recommendations.problem: Both shipped examples hardcode local file paths (data/ukbppp_pcsk9_full_window.tsv, 1kg_EUR/EUR) with no bundled or synthetic data, so neither can be executed without the user's own real data or an auditor-built substitute.
recommendations.root_cause: Examples are written as illustrative code patterns rather than self-contained, runnable smoke tests.
recommendations.fix: Bundle a small synthetic dataset (as this audit built) alongside each example so an agent can run it directly to verify the pattern before substituting real data.
